transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because... lately I've been really focused on my face. We recently put in a brighter bathroom mirror at home, and ever since we did that, I just keep noticing that the skin around my cheeks and my jaw looks uneven, or kind of saggy to me. My husband says he can’t really see what I’m talking about, but it's really been on my mind.
Do you repeatedly check your face in mirrors because of this concern?

Yeah, I do. Most mornings, I end up checking my face from a few different angles in that mirror. I usually put on a little extra makeup before I leave for the courthouse, just to try and smooth things out. 

And... well, I guess I also catch myself comparing my face to the other women I see at work. I even try to avoid being in any casual pictures if I’m just not feeling okay about how I look that day.
Are you mainly worried that your face looks unattractive, rather than that these changes might be a sign of a medical problem?

Yeah, exactly. I'm not... I don't think it's a medical issue or that I'm sick or anything like that. It's really just about how it looks. I just worry that it makes me look older and, well, unattractive. That's really the only thing I'm worried about.
About how much time each day do you spend thinking about or checking your appearance?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I've never actually timed it. 

It's mostly just that extra time in the morning when I'm getting ready for work, and then maybe... I don't know, a few quick checks if I use the restroom at the courthouse during the day. I'm definitely not standing in front of a mirror for hours at a time or anything like that. It just kind of pops into my head on and off.
How much does worrying about your facial appearance interfere with your work, relationships, or daily activities?

It doesn't completely stop me from doing things, but... well, it definitely gets in the way sometimes. Like, I still get all my work done at the firm, but because I spend that extra time getting ready in the morning, trying to fix things, I've ended up rushing into the courthouse a few times. And I've definitely missed the start of my yoga class more than once because of it. 

And socially... like I mentioned before about pictures, I've skipped being in a few casual photos at my book club and some community events. I just didn't want to have to worry about how my face was going to look in them. So, it's not ruining my life, but it's definitely a nuisance.
